title: “Sibling Rivalry" SCA Shabbat Message by Yola Ashkenazi
summary: This class by Yola Ashkenazi explores Parasha Tessaveh, focusing on the absence of Moshe's name and how the relationship between Moshe and Aaron represents a turning point in the sibling dynamics of the Torah. Drawing on Sefer Bereshit and an idea from Rabbi Sachs, the speaker contrasts earlier brotherly rivalries with the cooperative leadership of Moshe and Aaron, concluding with a message about treating family and siblings with respect.
questions: Why is Moshe's name completely absent from Parasha Tessaveh?
How does the relationship between Moshe and Aaron differ from sibling rivalries in Sefer Bereshit?
What role did Aaron's lack of jealousy play in his worthiness to be Kohen Gadol?
What lesson can we learn from Moshe and Aaron regarding our own family relationships?
